title: Space Mining | The Future or Science Fiction?
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 哈喽，哈喽哈喽，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 出品的英语学习播客《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: The show where you can listen to fascinating stories, and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你可以聆听精彩绝伦的故事，了解这个世界稀奇古怪、美妙绝伦的事物，同时还能提升你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about space mining.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要聊一聊太空采矿。

sentences.en: It’s the idea that we can mine valuable minerals not from Earth, but from space.
sentences.zh: 这个概念指的是，我们开采珍贵矿产不是从地球上开采，而是从太空中获取。

sentences.en: So in this episode we’ll talk about why some people are so excited about it, how and why it could work, some of its major challenges, and ask ourselves whether it will ever go from the realm of science fiction to reality.
sentences.zh: 所以在本期节目中，我们将讨论为什么有些人对此兴奋不已、它如何能够以及为何能够行得通、它所面临的一些重大挑战，并探讨它究竟会从科幻小说的领域变成现实，还是只停留在幻想中。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s get started and talk about space mining.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们开始吧，来聊聊太空采矿。

sentences.en: The 19th century was an exciting time in terms of space observation.
sentences.zh: 对于太空观测而言，19世纪是一个激动人心的时代。

sentences.en: The first asteroid, Ceres, was spotted in 1801 by the Italian astronomer Giuseppe Piazzi.
sentences.zh: 1801年，意大利天文学家朱塞佩·皮亚齐发现了第一颗小行星谷神星。

sentences.en: Half a century later, his countryman Annibale de Gasparis was working in his observatory in Naples.
sentences.zh: 半个世纪后，他的同胞安尼巴莱·德加斯帕里斯正在那不勒斯的天文台工作。

sentences.en: He saw an asteroid that he named 16 Psyche, after the Greek goddess of the soul.
sentences.zh: 他发现了一颗小行星，并以希腊神话中灵魂女神的名字将其命名为 16 Psyche（灵神星）。

sentences.en: Now, this was just one of 9 different asteroids that he discovered.
sentences.zh: 这其实只是他发现的 9 颗不同小行星中的一颗。

sentences.en: To him, it probably looked like a giant rock, an important scientific discovery, but not much more than that.
sentences.zh: 对当时的他说来，这可能只是一块巨大的岩石，是一项重要的科学发现，但也仅此而已了。

sentences.en: However, modern astronomers believe 16 Psyche to be immeasurably more valuable than was first thought.
sentences.zh: 然而，现代天文学家认为，16 Psyche 的价值比最初想象的要不可估量得多。

sentences.en: To be precise, this asteroid is thought to contain precious metals worth 10 quintillion dollars.
sentences.zh: 准确地说，这颗小行星据信包含价值高达 10 京（10 quintillion）美元的贵金属。

sentences.en: A quintillion might sound like a made-up number, something that a child might say like a gazillion or a bazillion, which I should add are not real numbers.
sentences.zh: “京”（quintillion）听起来像是一个捏造出来的数字，就像小孩子可能会说的“gazillion”或“bazillion”那样——我得补充一下，这些都不是真正的数字。

sentences.en: But a quintillion is not made-up, it is just so big that you’ve probably never heard of it.
sentences.zh: 但 quintillion 并不是凭空捏造的，它只是数额太大了，以至于你可能从未听说过它。

sentences.en: 10 quintillion is 10, followed by 19 zeroes.
sentences.zh: 10京就是 10 后面加上 19 个零。

sentences.en: Or to put it another way, it is 10,000 trillion, 100 times the value of the entire global economy.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它是 10,000 万亿，相当于整个全球经济总产值的 100 倍。

sentences.en: And it is right up there, in space, floating around, with nobody guarding it.
sentences.zh: 它就静静地待在太空中，四处漂浮，而且没有任何人看守。

sentences.en: And not just 16 Psyche. There are millions of asteroids, some large, some small, many of which are believed to contain enough precious minerals to supply humanity for literally millions of years.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是 16 Psyche。太空中数以百万计的小行星，有大有小，其中许多据信蕴含着足够的珍贵矿产，足以为人类提供整整数百万年的消耗。

sentences.en: So, what if there were a way to go up there and simply take them?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果有一种方法能够去到那里并直接把它们拿回来呢？

sentences.en: This is the story of space mining, or asteroid mining to be precise.
sentences.zh: 这就是太空采矿的故事，准确地说是小行星采矿的故事。

sentences.en: To some, it seems like science fiction, a fixation on looking to space while we have more than enough problems to deal with back on Earth.
sentences.zh: 在有些人看来，这就像是科幻小说，是一门只会仰望星空、却对地球上亟待解决的成堆问题视而不见的执念。

sentences.en: But to others it is something that can and will become reality, and a way to solve many of the problems we have on Earth by taking what already exists in space.
sentences.zh: 但对另一些人来说，这是能够而且终将成为现实的事情，也是通过利用太空中现有的资源来解决地球上许多问题的一种途径。

sentences.en: So, let’s start with some definitions. Asteroids are objects that orbit the sun, much like planets, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, and so on.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们从一些定义开始。小行星是围绕太阳运行的天体，这一点很像行星，比如地球、火星、木星等等。

sentences.en: They are essentially remnants of the early solar system, chunks of rock and metal that never formed into planets.
sentences.zh: 它们本质上是早期太阳系的残余物，是没有形成行星的岩石和金属块。

sentences.en: The difference between an asteroid and a planet mainly comes down to size.
sentences.zh: 小行星和行星的区别主要在于大小。

sentences.en: Planets are much bigger, therefore have a larger gravitational pull, and are circular in shape, because of gravity.
sentences.zh: 行星要大得多，因此具有更强的引力，而且在引力的作用下呈圆形。

sentences.en: Asteroids are smaller, typically ranging from a few hundred metres or so through to the largest known asteroid, which is almost 1,000 kilometres in diameter, around the same width as France from its most northern to most southern point.
sentences.zh: 小行星较小，直径通常从几百米不等，一直到已知最大的一颗小行星——它的直径接近 1,000 公里，大致相当于法国从最北端到最南端的宽度。

sentences.en: It’s pretty big, but it’s much smaller than a planet.
sentences.zh: 它挺大的，但比行星小得多。

sentences.en: And because they are much smaller, they have a much lower gravitational pull, so they’re not typically round but more like a rock.
sentences.zh: 正因为它们小得多，所以引力也小得多，因此它们通常不是圆的，而是更像一块普通的岩石。

sentences.en: Most known asteroids are in the asteroid belt, which is between Mars and Jupiter, but not all; there are others that come closer to Earth.
sentences.zh: 大多数已知的小行星都位于火星和木星之间的小行星带中，但并非全部；还有其他一些小行星会更靠近地球。

sentences.en: Some come too close, like the one that is thought to have hit Earth and wiped out the dinosaurs 66 million years ago.
sentences.zh: 有些靠得太近了，就像那颗被认为在 6600 万年前撞击地球并导致恐龙灭绝的小行星一样。

sentences.en: Fortunately, we humans are better than dinosaurs at spotting potential threats in the sky, so in the event of an asteroid looking like it was on a collision path with Earth, we would know about it pretty quickly and be more capable than a diplodocus of changing its trajectory.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，我们人类比恐龙更善于发现天空中潜在的威胁，所以如果真的有小行星看起来正处于与地球相撞的轨道上，我们能很快察觉到，并且比梁龙更有能力去改变它的运行轨迹。

sentences.en: So, we know where asteroids are, and because they orbit the sun, it is fairly easy to model their position at any point in time.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们知道小行星在哪里，而且因为它们绕太阳运行，模拟它们在任何时间点的位置其实相当容易。

sentences.en: And while 19th-century astronomers might not have known much about the consistency of an asteroid, or what it is actually made out of, we now do.
sentences.zh: 虽然 19 世纪的天文学家可能对小行星的稠密度或它的实际成分知之甚少，但我们现在知道了。

sentences.en: Some asteroids are thought to contain incredibly high levels of precious metals.
sentences.zh: 有些小行星被认为含有极其高含量的贵金属。

sentences.en: When the solar system was formed, heavy elements like gold, platinum, nickel, and iron were distributed throughout the massive cloud of gas and dust that eventually became the Sun and the planets.
sentences.zh: 当太阳系形成时，金、铂、镍和铁等重元素分布在最终形成太阳和行星的庞大气体和尘土云中。

sentences.en: These elements were created during supernova explosions and collisions of neutron stars—cosmic events that forge the universe’s heaviest and most valuable materials.
sentences.zh: 这些元素是在超新星爆炸和中子星碰撞过程中产生的——这些宇宙事件锻造出了宇宙中最重、最有价值的物质。

sentences.en: When the solar system began to take shape, gravity caused much of the heavy material to sink towards the cores of the newly forming planets.
sentences.zh: 当太阳系开始成形时，引力导致大部分重物质下沉到新形成行星的核心。

sentences.en: On Earth, for example, most of the gold and platinum we know of is thought to be buried deep within the planet’s core, out of reach for humans.
sentences.zh: 例如，在地球上，我们所知的大部分黄金和铂金都被认为埋藏在地球核心深处，人类根本够不到。

sentences.en: But not all of this material ended up inside planets.
sentences.zh: 但并非所有这些物质最终都落入了行星内部。

sentences.en: Some of it remained as loose chunks of rock and metal scattered throughout the solar system—what we now call asteroids.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分作为松散的岩石和金属块残留在太阳系各处——也就是我们现在所说的小行星。

sentences.en: These asteroids are essentially the leftover building blocks of planets, and many contain high concentrations of metals that didn’t make it into planetary cores.
sentences.zh: 这些小行星本质上是行星遗留的积木，许多都含有高浓度的、未能进入行星核心的金属。

sentences.en: But what makes these asteroids so appealing isn’t just their high metal content—it’s that the metals are often much more accessible than on Earth.
sentences.zh: 但这些小行星如此吸引人的地方，不仅仅是因为它们的高金属含量——而是因为这些金属往往比地球上的更容易获取。

sentences.en: Unlike Earth, where heavy metals have sunk to the core, asteroids haven’t undergone the same processes of differentiation.
sentences.zh: 与地球上重金属已经下沉到地核的情况不同，小行星没有经历过同样的熔融分异过程。

sentences.en: This means that their metals are distributed throughout their structure, making them, in theory at least, easier to extract.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它们的金属分布在整个结构中，理论上讲，这使得它们更容易开采。

sentences.en: As I’m sure you will know, mining almost anything on Earth, and especially mining precious metals, is a dirty, intensive and expensive activity, often carried out by people, sometimes even children, working in pretty awful conditions.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定大家都知道，在地球上开采任何东西，尤其是开采贵金属，都是一项肮脏、劳民伤财且昂贵的活动，而且往往是由那些甚至包括儿童在内、在相当恶劣的条件下工作的人来完成的。

sentences.en: Cobalt, for example, is a vital part of electric batteries, and 70% of all cobalt is produced in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
sentences.zh: 例如，钴是电池中不可或缺的重要部分，而全球 70% 的钴都产自刚果民主共和国。

sentences.en: And conditions in the Congolese cobalt mines have been likened to modern-day slavery.
sentences.zh: 刚果钴矿里的工作条件甚至被比作现代奴隶制。

sentences.en: Cobalt and Congo are just one example. Getting anything out of the Earth’s crust is an intensive, polluting process, so wouldn’t it be better, the argument goes, for us just to take it from an asteroid?
sentences.zh: 钴和刚果只是一个例子。从地壳中开采任何东西都是一个高耗能、高污染的过程，所以，照此逻辑，我们直接从一颗小行星上获取不是更好吗？

sentences.en: There would be no pollution, no child labour, and no destruction of forests to make way for the mines.
sentences.zh: 那样就不会有污染，没有童工，也不会为了腾出矿区而破坏森林。

sentences.en: In theory, it all sounds very positive. A lifetime’s supply of precious metals floating around in the sky, fortunes to be made for anyone who can find a way to go up there and get them.
sentences.zh: 从理论上讲，这一切听起来非常美好。用之不竭的贵金属漂浮在太空中，只要谁能找到办法去那里把它们弄回来，就能获得巨额财富。

sentences.en: Of course, it's more complicated than that.
sentences.zh: 当然，实际情况要复杂得多。

sentences.en: First, let’s talk about the practicality of getting to an asteroid.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们来谈谈前往小行星的实际可行性。

sentences.en: They are a long way away. In late 2023 NASA did actually send a mission to the asteroid Psyche, the one I mentioned at the start of the episode.
sentences.zh: 它们离得很远。在 2023 年底，美国宇航局（NASA）确实向节目开头提到的那颗名为“灵神星”（Psyche）的小行星发射了一次探测任务。

sentences.en: Its scheduled arrival date is 2029, so it will take 6 years for it to get there.
sentences.zh: 它预定的到达日期是 2029 年，这意味着它需要花 6 年时间才能抵达。

sentences.en: It’s travelling at something like 50,000 kilometres an hour, incredibly fast by Earth standards, the problem is that it needs to travel almost 500 million kilometres to get there.
sentences.zh: 它正以每小时大约 5 万公里的速度飞行，按地球标准来看这已经快得难以置信了，但问题是它需要飞行将近 5 亿公里才能到达目的地。

sentences.en: And it isn’t on a space mining mission, but rather a fact-gathering one.
sentences.zh: 而且这不是一次太空采矿任务，而是一次收集信息的任务。

sentences.en: No spacecraft has ever been to Psyche before, so the plan is to go and observe it.
sentences.zh: 此前没有任何飞船去过 Psyche，所以计划是去实地观测它。

sentences.en: Given the cost of getting to an asteroid, any mission needs to be fairly sure that it will find what it’s looking for, and given that not all asteroids are created equal–some are rocky, others are icy, and others contain high levels of precious metals–you need to send a fact-finding mission first before committing to a mining mission.
sentences.zh: 考虑到前往小行星的高昂成本，任何任务都需要有相当大的把握确保能找到所寻找的东西，而且鉴于并非所有小行星生来平等——有些是岩石质的，有些是冰质的，还有些含有高含量的贵金属——在承诺进行采矿任务之前，你需要先派出一趟事实勘察任务。

sentences.en: Now, let’s talk about costs. A large proportion of the cost of any space mission is getting out of the Earth’s atmosphere, and then returning safely.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们来谈谈成本。任何太空任务的大部分成本都花在突破地球大气层以及安全返回上。

sentences.en: Sending something to space is expensive, but it is considerably cheaper than it used to be.
sentences.zh: 把东西送上太空价格不菲，但比过去要便宜多了。

sentences.en: During the first thirty years or so of space launches, it would typically cost in the region of $25,000 per kilo to send something to space, but some projects were upwards of $100,000 per kilo.
sentences.zh: 在太空发射的前三十年左右，把东西送上太空通常花费大约每公斤 25,000 美元，有些项目甚至超过每公斤 100,000 美元。

sentences.en: Companies such as SpaceX have been hyper-focused on reducing the cost of going to space so that it now costs around $1,500 per kilo.
sentences.zh: 像 SpaceX 这样的公司一直高度专注于降低太空旅行的成本，以至于现在成本已经降到了每公斤大约 1,500 美元。

sentences.en: But with reusable rockets and increasing efficiencies in every part of the launch process, there are some estimates that this could be brought down to around $10 per kilo, less than it would cost to send a 1 kilo parcel within the UK.
sentences.zh: 但是随着可重复使用火箭的使用以及发射流程各个环节效率的提高，有一些估计表明，这一成本甚至可以降至每公斤 10 美元左右，这比在英国境内寄一个 1 公斤的包裹还要便宜。

sentences.en: So, yes, going to space and therefore getting to an asteroid is very expensive, but while a few decades ago it would have been so expensive that it simply wouldn’t have been economically viable, now it very well might be.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，去太空从而到达小行星是非常昂贵的，但几十年前，这种费用高昂到根本不具备经济可行性，而现在，它完全有可能实现了。

sentences.en: So, let’s assume that costs have gone down to such an extent that the first asteroid mining mission is ready for lift-off.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们假设成本已经大幅下降，以至于第一次小行星采矿任务已经准备好点火升空了。

sentences.en: How would it work? Well, there are several fundamental differences between Earth and Space that mean an asteroid mine certainly wouldn’t bear much resemblance to any mine on Earth.
sentences.zh: 它将如何运作呢？嗯，地球和太空之间存在几个根本性的差异，这意味着太空采矿场绝对不会跟地球上的任何矿场有太多相似之处。

sentences.en: Obviously, there is the problem of how to get all of the equipment there, so it simply wouldn’t be possible to boost large trucks and heavy equipment into space, and anyhow, this kind of equipment would probably be of little use on an asteroid.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，首先面临的是如何把所有设备运到那里的问题，将大型卡车和重型设备运推上太空是根本不可能实现的，而且无论如何，这类设备在小行星上可能也没多大用处。

sentences.en: There is no gravity on an asteroid, so everything would need to be tied down to the asteroid.
sentences.zh: 小行星上没有引力，所以所有的东西都必须绑在小行星上。

sentences.en: Most probably, there would be some kind of great canopy, a tent-like structure, that was put over the area that was being mined, otherwise, all of the dust and precious metals would simply blow away into space.
sentences.zh: 最有可能的情况是，会有某种巨大的天篷、类似于帐篷的结构，被搭建在正在开采的区域上方，否则，所有的尘埃和贵金属都会直接被吹进太空中。

sentences.en: And in terms of the mining process, there are several different ideas about how this could work.
sentences.zh: 在开采工艺方面，关于这该如何运作有几种不同的设想。

sentences.en: Perhaps it would be lasers that would vaporise material, robotic arms that grind and collect it, or even specialised bacteria, as they do in terrestrial biomining, that break down rock and release valuable metals like nickel or cobalt.
sentences.zh: 也许会使用激光来汽化物质，用机械臂来研磨和收集，或者甚至像地面生物浸出那样使用特殊的细菌来分解岩石并释放出镍或钴等有价值的金属。

sentences.en: Another significant challenge is that asteroids typically rotate, often unpredictably and at varying speeds.
sentences.zh: 另一个重大挑战是小行星通常会旋转，而且往往是毫无规律地以不同的速度旋转。

sentences.en: This constant movement makes it very difficult to safely land equipment, maintain stability, or accurately mine materials.
sentences.zh: 这种持续的运动使得安全降落设备、维持稳定性或精确开采物资变得极其困难。

sentences.en: To address this, the mining team would need to find some way of stabilising the asteroid, keeping it in position.
sentences.zh: 为了解决这个问题，采矿团队需要找到某种使小行星稳定下来、将其固定在原位的方法。

sentences.en: Maybe this would be using thrusters to slow or stop its rotation.
sentences.zh: 也许这可以通过使用推进器来减缓或停止其旋转来实现。

sentences.en: Maybe it would be by using large nets or tethers to anchor it, or by synchronising mining tools to match the asteroid’s rotation.
sentences.zh: 也许可以通过使用大网或系绳来锚定它，或者通过同步采矿工具来配合小行星的旋转来实现。

sentences.en: And then there is the question of who would work on the mine.
sentences.zh: 接下来就是谁来矿上工作的问题了。

sentences.en: This is not a question of whether there would be thousands of astronauts with hammers and shovels physically digging the surface themselves, and lugging large sacks back at the end of the day, but rather whether the mine would be 100% automated, controlled from back on Earth or from a space mission closer to Earth, or whether there would be human astronauts monitoring the situation from the site, just in case anything went wrong.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说会有成千上万的宇航员拿着锤子和铁锹亲自在表面挖掘，最后背着大麻袋回来，而是说这个矿场会是 100% 自动化的，由地球后方或距离地球更近的太空任务进行控制，亦或是会有宇航员在现场监控情况以防万一出现任何差错。

sentences.en: And there is also the legal question. One of the very first episodes we ever made, more than 5 years ago now, was about the question of who owns space.
sentences.zh: 同时还有一个法律问题。我们在 5 年多前制作的第一批节目之一，探讨的就是“谁拥有太空”这个问题。

sentences.en: 5 years on, that question still remains largely unanswered.
sentences.zh: 5 年过去了，这个问题在很大程度上依然没有答案。

sentences.en: The first principle of the 1967 Space Treaty is, and I’m quoting directly, “the exploration and use of outer space shall be carried out for the benefit and in the interests of all countries and shall be the province of all mankind”.
sentences.zh: 1967 年《外层空间条约》的第一条原则是——我在这里直接引用——“探索和利用外层空间应为所有国家谋福利和利益，并属于全人类的省份。”

sentences.en: And it is shortly followed by “outer space is not subject to national appropriation by claim of sovereignty, by means of use or occupation, or by any other means”.
sentences.zh: 紧接着后面的一句是：“外层空间不得通过提出主权要求、通过使用或占有或通过任何其他方式据为己有。”

sentences.en: In other words, nobody owns space. But there is a grey area over what this means in terms of asteroid mining.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，没有人拥有太空。但对于这在小行星采矿方面意味着什么，目前还存在一个灰色地带。

sentences.en: If a company successfully mines an asteroid, who owns the minerals they mine?
sentences.zh: 如果一家公司成功开采了一颗小行星，他们开采出的矿产归谁所有？

sentences.en: Is it a bit like fishing, where any boat can fish in international waters, and they are free to use and sell what they catch?
sentences.zh: 这是否有点像捕鱼，任何船只都可以在国际水域捕鱼，并且可以自由使用和出售他们捕获的东西？

sentences.en: Or is it not? In 2015, Barack Obama signed something called the SPACE Act, which gives U.S. citizens the right to "engage in the commercial exploration and exploitation of 'space resources' [including... water and minerals] ".
sentences.zh: 还是说并不是这样？2015 年，贝拉克·奥巴马签署了一项名为《太空法案》的文件，赋予了美国公民“从事‘太空资源’[包括……水和矿物]商业勘探和开发的权利”。

sentences.en: In other words, US citizens can do it, according to US law at least.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，至少根据美国法律，美国公民可以这么做。

sentences.en: But how does this law play with international law?
sentences.zh: 但这套法律又该如何与国际法相协调呢？

sentences.en: It hasn’t been an issue so far, because nobody has done it, but if asteroid mining turns from the theoretical to the practical, it is a question that will need to be addressed.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止这还不是个问题，因为还没有人这么做过，但如果小行星采矿从理论变成现实，这将是一个必须解决的问题。

sentences.en: Now, let’s assume that it is addressed, and that companies are able to build cost-effective ways of getting mining equipment to space, and successfully mining an asteroid.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们假设这个问题得到了解决，各公司能够构建出划算的方案将采矿设备送上太空，并成功开采一颗小行星。

sentences.en: What happens next? Well, there is also the question of where the minerals go.
sentences.zh: 接下来会发生什么？嗯，还有一个问题是这些矿物该去往何处。

sentences.en: One option is to bring them back to Earth and use them here.
sentences.zh: 一种选择是将它们带回地球并在本地使用。

sentences.en: We need the minerals found on asteroids, especially the platinum group metals, we need them here on Earth, for everything from batteries to solar panels to electric cars, so there is a clear demand.
sentences.zh: 我们需要小行星上发现的矿物，尤其是铂族金属，我们在地球上需要它们，用于从电池到太阳能电池板再到电动汽车的方方面面，因此存在着明确的需求。

sentences.en: Whoever can bring them back cost effectively will become spectacularly wealthy.
sentences.zh: 谁能把它们划算地带回来，谁就会变得富可敌国。

sentences.en: But the other option is to leave them in space, for use in space.
sentences.zh: 但另一个选择是把它们留在太空中，在太空里使用。

sentences.en: The more activity there is in space, the more stuff is needed, and this currently all needs to be brought from Earth and then sent to space, which is expensive.
sentences.zh: 太空中的活动越多，需要的东西就越多，而目前这些东西都需要从地球采购然后运往太空，这代价高昂。

sentences.en: No matter how plentiful and cheap something might be on Earth, in space it suddenly becomes very expensive.
sentences.zh: 无论某种东西在地球上多么充裕、多么便宜，到了太空中它突然就变得极为昂贵。

sentences.en: One obvious example is water. A kilo of water might be practically free on Earth, but taking a kilo of water to space costs the same as taking a kilo of anything else to space.
sentences.zh: 一个明显的例子就是水。一公斤水在地球上可能几乎是免费的，但把一公斤水带到太空的成本和把任何其他东西带到太空的成本是一样的。

sentences.en: And in space, water is incredibly important and in short supply.
sentences.zh: 而在太空中，水极其重要且严重短缺。

sentences.en: Water is needed to keep astronauts hydrated, as well as for cooling and regulating the temperature of a spacecraft, and as a radiation shield.
sentences.zh: 我们需要水来保证宇航员的水分供应，用于冷却和调节航天器的温度，以及作为辐射屏蔽层。

sentences.en: But perhaps even more important than this are the component parts of water; hydrogen and oxygen.
sentences.zh: 但也许比这更重要的是水的组成部分：氢和氧。

sentences.en: Liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen are the primary propellants of many modern rockets, so if water can be found on an asteroid, for example, it becomes incredibly valuable.
sentences.zh: 液氢和液氧是许多现代火箭的主要推进剂，所以如果在小行星上发现了水，它就会变得极其宝贵。

sentences.en: There are no petrol stations in space, all fuel needs to be brought up from Earth, but if a source of water, in the form of ice or water-rich material, could be found, and this could be processed in space into rocket fuel and left in space, where it is most useful and valuable, then this would be like a petrol station in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中没有加油站，所有的燃料都需要从地球运上去，但如果能找到水的来源——以冰或富水物质的形式——并且能在太空中将其加工成火箭燃料并留在太空中（那正是它最有用、最有价值的地方），那么这就相当于在太空中建了一个加油站。

sentences.en: It would bring down the cost of space launches, because they wouldn’t have to take so much fuel up from Earth, and it would allow for longer and faster journeys within space.
sentences.zh: 这将降低太空发射的成本，因为他们不必从地球携带那么多的燃料，并将使太空中的长途和快速航行成为可能。

sentences.en: And perhaps veering even more into the realms of the ultra-futuristic, in a universe in which there were settlements on other planets, Mars, for example, it makes much more sense to manufacture what is needed in space rather than on Earth.
sentences.zh: 如果再往超级未来主义的方向延伸一点，在一个存在其他星球定居点的宇宙中——比如火星，在太空中制造所需的东西比在地球上制造要合理得多。

sentences.en: If you need to build a settlement, it could be a lot more cost effective to take the raw materials from a nearby asteroid than shooting them up from a rocket on Earth.
sentences.zh: 如果你需要建立一个定居点，从附近的小行星获取原材料，要比用地球上的火箭发射成本划算得多。

sentences.en: So, one option is to leave the mined materials in space.
sentences.zh: 所以，一种选择是将开采出来的材料留在太空中。

sentences.en: But what would happen if these rare minerals were brought back down to Earth?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果把这些稀有矿物带回地球，会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: You heard at the start that just one asteroid contains precious metals worth 100 times the entire global economy, enough for every person on Earth to receive around $1.25 billion, so what would be the impact of that?
sentences.zh: 你刚才在开头听说了，仅一颗小行星就包含价值相当于整个全球经济 100 倍的贵金属，足以让地球上的每个人分到大约 12.5 亿美元，那么这会产生什么影响呢？

sentences.en: Well, everyone on Earth wouldn’t receive $1.25 billion.
sentences.zh: 嗯，地球上的每个人其实并不会拿到 1.25 亿美元。

sentences.en: This 10 quintillion dollar number is the estimated total value of all the precious metals in that asteroid at current market prices.
sentences.zh: 这 10 京美元的数字是根据当前市场价格估算的那颗小行星上所有贵金属的总价值。

sentences.en: If it were all brought back to Earth at once, it would flood the market, and the price would come crashing down because we would have more iron, platinum and cobalt than we knew what to do with.
sentences.zh: 如果一下子把它们全带回地球，市场就会崩盘，价格也会一落千丈，因为我们拥有的铁、铂和钴将多得不知该拿它们怎么办。

sentences.en: But that isn’t going to happen. Because of the timelines of getting there, the cost of a mission, and the fact that a spacecraft is limited to how much it can carry back, it would take hundreds if not thousands of years for even a fraction of the precious metals on an asteroid this size to be mined and then brought back to Earth.
sentences.zh: 但这不会发生。考虑到到达那里的时间表、任务成本，以及飞船运回货物的容量限制，即使开采和带回这样体量的小行星上的贵金属中的一小部分，也需要几百年甚至几千年。

sentences.en: Still, there are some commentators who have pointed out that, even with a relatively small haul of precious metals, asteroid mining could be very detrimental to lower-income countries that have so-far relied on natural resource extraction.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，一些评论员指出，即使带着相对较少量的贵金属，小行星采矿也可能对迄今为止一直依赖自然资源开采的低收入国家造成极大损害。

sentences.en: Mines back on Earth would be closed, millions of people would be out of a job, and there would need to be some sort of mechanism for these countries to be compensated by the countries or companies that enjoyed the spoils of asteroid mining.
sentences.zh: 地球上的矿山将会关闭，成百上千万人将失去工作，而且需要建立某种机制，由享受小行星采矿战果的国家或公司向这些国家提供补偿。

sentences.en: There are also environmental concerns, but these are mainly the concerns about space pollution, of debris from the mines floating around in space.
sentences.zh: 此外还有环境问题，但这些主要是关于太空污染的担忧，也就是矿山碎片在太空中四处漂浮的问题。

sentences.en: In terms of environmental concerns on Earth, it seems pretty clear-cut.
sentences.zh: 就地球上的环境问题而言，情况似乎相当明了。

sentences.en: Yes, sending a rocket into space and then bringing it back into the atmosphere releases a lot of CO2, but these are the only significant emissions that would be caused by space mining.
sentences.zh: 是的，把火箭送入太空然后让它重返大气层会释放大量的二氧化碳，但这将是太空采矿所造成的唯一重大排放。

sentences.en: According to one study, mining a kilo of platinum from an asteroid would result in around 60 kilogrammes of CO2, and this is against 40,000 kilogrammes of CO2 to get every kilo of platinum out of the Earth’s crust like we do today.
sentences.zh: 根据一项研究，从小行星上开采一公斤铂金将产生大约 60 公斤的二氧化碳，而相比之下，像我们今天这样从地壳中开采每一公斤铂金则需要产生 40,000 公斤的二氧化碳。

sentences.en: In other words, yes, you might think of a rocket blasting off into space and think, “Well, that must be very environmentally unfriendly”, but it is approximately 700 times better for the environment than the way we currently do it.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，是的，你可能会想到火箭呼啸着飞向太空，然后觉得“嗯，这一定很不环保”，但它对环境的友好程度大约是我们目前开采方式的 700 倍。

sentences.en: So, if it all sounds so good in theory, why is it not already happening?
sentences.zh: 那么，既然这一切在理论上听起来这么棒，为什么它现在还没有发生呢？

sentences.en: It comes down to money. Building all of the technology, actually figuring out how to do it, and then doing test after test after test will require hundreds of billions of dollars in investment.
sentences.zh: 归根结底还是钱的问题。构建所有的技术、真正弄清楚如何做到这一点，然后进行一次又一次又一次的测试，将需要数千亿美元的投资。

sentences.en: And with no certain return. Several companies have started this process, but none have made the progress that they had initially promised.
sentences.zh: 而且还没有确定的回报。几家公司已经开始了这一进程，但没有一家取得了他们最初承诺的进展。

sentences.en: Most investors aren’t very good at being patient, especially when there is no guarantee of any return, and despite the huge potential prize, there is a lack of funding for asteroid mining companies.
sentences.zh: 大多数投资者并不擅长保持耐心，尤其是在没有任何回报保证的情况下，而且尽管潜力巨大，小行星采矿公司依然面临着资金缺乏的问题。

sentences.en: Still, as you listen to this episode, assuming that it isn’t the year 2029 yet, a NASA spacecraft is on its way to an asteroid that was first spotted in 1852, 16 Psyche.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，当你听到这期节目时，假设现在还不是 2029 年，美国宇航局的一艘航天器正开往一颗在 1852 年首次被发现的小行星——灵神星（16 Psyche）。

sentences.en: It will return with news, news that might just change the world.
sentences.zh: 它将带着消息返回，这些消息或许真的会改变世界。

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on space mining.
sentences.zh: 好了，这就是今天关于太空采矿的全部内容。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one, and that it might have given you a new perspective on the night sky.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目对你有所启发，并能让你对夜空产生全新的视角。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想知道你对这期节目的看法。

sentences.en: Did you know much about asteroid mining before?
sentences.zh: 在此之前，你对小行星采矿了解多少呢？

sentences.en: Do you think it is something that we will see in your lifetime?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是我们在有生之年能看到的事情吗？

sentences.en: You can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接进入我们的社区论坛，网址是 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他充满好奇心的人一起畅聊。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 出品的英语学习播客《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，注意安全，我们下期节目见。
